subject: health
title: Mastery check: problem size and support
essentialQuestion: How can understanding mental and emotional skills help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: A small problem may be handled with a pause and a plan; danger, repeated harm, or a problem that keeps disrupting daily life needs trusted-adult or professional support.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.
For problem size and support, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Create a menu of safe coping and support options for fictional scenarios.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about problem size and support. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in problem size and support; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the problem size and support task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits. Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options. Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media. Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
extensionChallenge: Apply problem size and support under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of problem size and support in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
